title: WTL Case Study: Starting a Five Beliefs Culture in a San Diego School
author: Stuart Jr., Dave
summary: Stuart Jr. presents a case study of lead teacher Rik Williams at Ocean View Christian Academy in San Diego, who translated The Will to Learn into a ninety-minute staff PD on student motivation that principal Angie Birney describes as a home run. He analyzes Rik's success through structural principles: one teacher who deeply owns the material leads the session, and that depth manifests as ease and credibility rather than mere information delivery; the session opens with a Valued Within move that lets teachers generate their own reasons the topic matters; and the framing situates the new idea within the school's existing instructional philosophy, preempting the 'one more thing' objection. Stuart Jr. then argues that a single excellent PD only starts the culture conversation — creating school-wide Five Key Beliefs culture requires sustained engagement over time, treating the framework not as an app to install but as an operating system to develop and internalize.
points: Effective school-wide PD on belief culture begins with one teacher who deeply owns the material — that depth produces the assured, easygoing manner and credibility that makes a session transformative rather than informational.

Opening with a Valued Within move — having teachers generate their own reasons the topic matters rather than receiving the presenter's arguments — displaces the 'one more thing' dynamic from the start.

Situating new ideas within the school's existing instructional philosophy signals coherence and reduces resistance; the PD is positioned as an extension of what teachers already believe, not an import.

A single home-run PD session can start a culture conversation, but the Five Key Beliefs become an operating system only through months of ongoing pondering, experimentation, and shared reflection among staff.

Schools do not need to wait for an outside expert to build this culture; a knowledgeable internal leader who owns the material and translates it to their specific setting can produce career-changing results.
quotes: Since The Will to Learn came out in spring of 2023, pockets of earnest educators have made it their own in delightful and admirable and powerful ways.

He didn't ask for a PD on a topic — he asked if he could do a PD on a topic. Then, he went about deeply learning the material. (The fruits of that deep learning were his "assured, easygoing manner" and "expertise.") The good news about The Will to Learn is that it's simple and deep.

A common teacher complaint with PD is that it's just "one more thing." The two moves Rik starts with mitigate this common (and valid) problem. First, the teachers come up with reasons why a PD on student motivation is Valuable. Then, Rik establishes that the PD topic is in line with the fundamental, pre-established imperatives of the school.

The thing with PDs like Rik's is that they start conversations around the Five Key Beliefs, but for these conversations to bear fruit, they need to keep going. Whenever I'm at work, my mind is constantly in conversation with itself about the Five Key Beliefs and how they work.

I've now said the thing (the book); how can schools take what I've said and make it their own, make it a living and breathing reality in their schools, make it not "one more thing" but just "this is how we approach helping students care about the work of learning?
